{{nymphs|parent=[[Caspia, Goddess of the Caspian Sea]]}}
Kurara is revered as the River Seraph of the Kura, a grand and mighty river that flows through the South Caucasus region, traversing through Georgia and Azerbaijan. Kurara is considered a divine being, a guardian and protector of the Kura River and the lands it blesses.

As the River Seraph, Kurara is often depicted as a majestic and ethereal figure, with a flowing gown that mirrors the shape and movement of the river. She is believed to have the power to regulate the flow of the river, to bestow fertility to the lands it irrigates, and to bless those who rely on its waters for sustenance and prosperity.

Kurara is also revered for her connection to the natural environment and the ecosystems along the Kura River. She is considered a protector of the flora and fauna that thrive in and around the river, and is often associated with the biodiversity and ecological balance that the Kura River supports.

Her name is spoken with reverence by those who live along the Kura River, and she is honored with rituals, prayers, and offerings, seeking her favor for a bountiful harvest, smooth navigation, and a harmonious relationship with the river and its surroundings. Kurara is considered a divine embodiment of the Kura River, commanding the respect and awe of those who recognize her as the sacred guardian of this vital waterway.
